waive.TypeOK: Shape check only: no behaviour change breaks it without also breaking a property above it.

mutations.name: id-change-silent
mutations.why: F3 as it was: the pool lets a window tab's file go on a session-id change without onSessionFilesChanged; another device's read in the gap becomes the snapshot and the later close says nothing.
mutations.equivalent: Since the host shares one numbered list, any read that finds the list changed publishes it and the delta goes to every device: the snapshot another device's read recorded can no longer hide a change from this one, so the F3 gap (listingChanged() silent on a session-id change) no longer leaves a device stale. The pool's announce stays (it is cheap and keeps the snapshot honest); the F3 unit tests still pin it.

mutations.name: drop-announce-on-close
mutations.why: A tab closing no longer calls listingChanged(): devices keep listing a released session as held.
mutations.search: /\ LET f2 == [file EXCEPT ![t] = NoS] IN file' = f2 /\ Announce(f2, rec)
mutations.replace: /\ LET f2 == [file EXCEPT ![t] = NoS] IN file' = f2 /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, evTimer>>

mutations.name: drop-announce-on-open
mutations.why: A tab opening a stored session no longer calls listingChanged(): devices miss that a tab holds it now.
mutations.search:
/\ file[t] = NoS /\ t \notin pendReg /\ nChanges < MaxChanges
    /\ LET f2 == [file EXCEPT ![t] = s] IN file' = f2 /\ Announce(f2, rec)
mutations.replace:
/\ file[t] = NoS /\ t \notin pendReg /\ nChanges < MaxChanges
    /\ LET f2 == [file EXCEPT ![t] = s] IN file' = f2 /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, evTimer>>

mutations.name: signature-ignores-openers
mutations.why: listingSignature compares only the held sessions: a closed-child record appearing or going changes no signature, so the host never reads and publishes it.
mutations.search: IF snap # Unk /\ Listing(f2, r2) # snap

mutations.name: snapshot-not-recorded-by-a-read
mutations.why: The host's reads stop recording #listingSnapshot: listingChanged() keeps returning early and never re-announces.

mutations.name: sameRow-ignores-heldOnHost
mutations.why: reconcile() keeps the old row when only heldOnHost differs (sameRow forgot the field): the window keeps its stale held flag.
mutations.replace: SetShow(d, new) == fshow' = [fshow EXCEPT ![d] = [s \in Sessions |-> IF fshow[d][s] # NoRow /\ new[s] # NoRow THEN [j |-> new[s].j, h |-> fshow[d][s].h, o |-> new[s].o] ELSE new[s]]]

mutations.name: sameRow-ignores-openedBySession
mutations.why: reconcile() keeps the old row when only openedBySession differs: the window keeps nesting a child under the wrong opener.
mutations.replace: SetShow(d, new) == fshow' = [fshow EXCEPT ![d] = [s \in Sessions |-> IF fshow[d][s] # NoRow /\ new[s] # NoRow THEN [j |-> new[s].j, h |-> new[s].h, o |-> fshow[d][s].o] ELSE new[s]]]

mutations.name: event-never-sent
mutations.why: The host's SESSIONS_CHANGED push (delta or bare) is dropped: a device never hears of a change after its first read.
mutations.search: EmitAll(l, m) == [d \in Devices |-> IF up[d] THEN Append(l[d], m) ELSE l[d]]

mutations.name: hsl-applies-on-mismatched-version
mutations.why: HostSessionList applies a change whose base is not the host version its copy holds (the guard `hostVersion === base` is gone): after a missed change it applies a delta to rows it was not made for.

mutations.name: feed-applies-on-mismatched-version
mutations.why: The window's feed applies a change whose base is not the version of its copy (`copy?.version === delta.base` is gone).

mutations.name: hsl-skips-reread-on-gap
mutations.why: HostSessionList ignores a change it cannot apply (a missed version) instead of marking its copy stale and telling the windows.
mutations.equivalent: The only way the computer's copy misses a version is a link drop (A6), and the link coming back marks the copy stale (LinkUp) before any later change could expose the gap; the gap branch repeats that. See link-up-does-not-mark-stale for the mutation that does make a missed version stick.

mutations.name: link-up-does-not-mark-stale
mutations.why: A link that came back does not mark the computer's copy of the host's list stale: the changes made while it was away stay missing until another change names a version the copy cannot apply.

mutations.name: hsl-ignores-announced-version
mutations.why: HostSessionList stops re-reading when a change named a later version than the answer it got (the finally branch of #read): on a link that reordered, the older answer would stay.
mutations.equivalent: On the in-order link a reply is never older than a change that reached the computer before it: the host's reply holds at least every version it sent before (publish sets the copy, then emits, then the reply is taken), so the branch never fires. MC_gap.cfg (LinkMode = gap) is the run where it matters, and there the copy fails anyway (F5).

mutations.name: feed-skips-reread-on-gap
mutations.why: The window's feed does not read again for a change it cannot apply (a missed version, or a bare event from a copy marked stale).

mutations.name: feed-ignores-announced-version
mutations.why: The feed forgets the version a change named while its read was under way: an answer older than that change stays on screen.

mutations.name: feed-applies-delta-during-read
mutations.why: The feed applies a change while its read is under way instead of noting its version: the older answer lands after it and overwrites it, a deleted row comes back.

mutations.name: lost-queued-refresh
mutations.why: A refresh asked for while a read was in flight is forgotten when the read lands: the last change never reaches the window.

mutations.name: refresh-while-in-flight-reads-again
mutations.why: refresh() starts another read while one is under way instead of queueing one: two asks at the device computer's copy.
mutations.search:
IN IF fin[d]
          THEN /\ fq' = [fq EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE] /\ need' = [need EXCEPT ![d] = n]
mutations.replace:
IN IF FALSE
          THEN /\ fq' = [fq EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE] /\ need' = [need EXCEPT ![d] = n]

mutations.name: delta-clears-stale
mutations.why: F4 as it was: an applied change marks the copy current, so a request's stale() is forgotten and the next ask answers from a copy that still lists what the request deleted.

mutations.name: no-stale-after-request
mutations.why: A delete, rename or move through a device no longer marks its copy of the host's list stale: the next ask answers from the copy before it.

mutations.name: stale-during-read-forgotten
mutations.why: A stale() that comes while a read of the host is under way is lost when the read lands: the read counts as fresher than the request it started before.
